title: Deuteronomy Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 15.

questions.question: How often are the Israelites commanded to make a release according to Deuteronomy 15?
options: Every seven years
Every year
Every ten years
Every five years
questions.correctAnswer: Every seven years
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:1 states that at the end of every seven years, thou shalt make a release.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 15, who must a creditor release debts to?
options: His neighbour and his brother
Only foreigners
Only strangers
His servants
questions.correctAnswer: His neighbour and his brother
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:2 commands every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it; he shall not exact it of his neighbour, or of his brother.

questions.question: Is a creditor allowed to exact a debt from a foreigner after the release year?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:3 says that of a foreigner thou mayest exact it again; but that which is thine with thy brother thine hand shall release.

questions.question: What condition is mentioned in Deuteronomy 15 that would affect there being no poor among you?
options: The LORD shall greatly bless thee in the land
The harvest is plentiful
The people obey the priests only
The enemies are defeated
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD shall greatly bless thee in the land
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:4 states that when there shall be no poor among you, for the LORD shall greatly bless thee in the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.

questions.question: What must one do to receive the blessings mentioned in Deuteronomy 15?
options: Carefully hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God and observe His commandments
Offer sacrifices daily
Build a temple
Gather wealth and store it
questions.correctAnswer: Carefully hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God and observe His commandments
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:5 instructs to carefully hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God, to observe all His commandments.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 15, what will happen if you obey God's commandments?
options: The LORD will bless you and you will lend to many nations without borrowing
You will be poor and oppressed
You will lose all your possessions
You will have no enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will bless you and you will lend to many nations without borrowing
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:6 says the LORD will bless thee as promised; thou shalt lend unto many nations, but shalt not borrow; and shalt reign over many nations.

questions.question: What are you instructed NOT to do to a poor man among your brethren in your land?
options: Harden your heart or shut your hand from him
Give him extra money
Ignore his requests
Send him away
questions.correctAnswer: Harden your heart or shut your hand from him
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:7 commands not to harden thine heart or shut thine hand from thy poor brother.

questions.question: What should you do for a poor brother according to Deuteronomy 15?
options: Open your hand wide and lend him sufficient for his need
Ignore him
Give him charity only once a year
Tell him to work harder
questions.correctAnswer: Open your hand wide and lend him sufficient for his need
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:8 instructs to open thine hand wide unto him and surely lend him sufficient for his need.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 15 warns not to have an evil eye against your poor brother when the year of release comes.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:9 warns against having an evil eye and withholding from the poor at the year of release.

questions.question: How should you feel when giving to the poor, according to Deuteronomy 15?
options: Your heart should not be grieved
You should feel reluctant
You should give only if forced
You should give secretly
questions.correctAnswer: Your heart should not be grieved
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:10 states that thou shalt surely give and thine heart shall not be grieved when thou givest unto him.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 15, why must the poor never cease out of the land?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:11 states the poor shall never cease, so the command to open your hand wide to your poor brother is given. It is a fact that the poor will always be present, not that they should never cease.

questions.question: Which of these instructions appears first in Deuteronomy 15?
options: Make a release every seven years
Lend to the poor generously
Sanctify firstlings of your herd
Free Hebrew servants after six years
questions.correctAnswer: Make a release every seven years
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:1 begins with the command to make a release at the end of every seven years, before other instructions.

questions.question: True or False: If you have a poor brother in your gates, you may shut your hand from him according to Deuteronomy 15.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:7 explicitly says thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother.

questions.question: Who is called the LORD'S release in Deuteronomy 15?
options: The release of debts between neighbors and brothers
The release of animals
The release of servants
The release of offerings
questions.correctAnswer: The release of debts between neighbors and brothers
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:2 explains that releasing debts to neighbors and brothers is called the LORD'S release.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 15, what is promised if you obey the LORD and observe His commandments?
options: You shall lend to many nations and not borrow
You shall never face poverty
You shall live without any enemies
You shall become a king
questions.correctAnswer: You shall lend to many nations and not borrow
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:6 promises that the LORD will bless thee, and thou shalt lend unto many nations but shalt not borrow.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What warning does Deuteronomy 15:9 give about attitudes toward the poor in the year of release?
options: Do not harbor an evil thought to withhold help because it is the year of release
Make sure to collect all debts before the year of release
Ignore the poor during the year of release since debts are cancelled
Only give to foreigners, not to poor brethren
questions.correctAnswer: Do not harbor an evil thought to withhold help because it is the year of release
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:9 warns against having an evil heart thinking that since the year of release is near, one should withhold giving to the poor brother, as this would be sin and cause the poor to cry to the LORD. This complements the call in verses 7-8 to be generous to the poor.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 15:10, how should one feel when giving to the poor?
options: Reluctant but obligated
Grieved and sorrowful
Joyful and without grief
Indifferent and detached
questions.correctAnswer: Joyful and without grief
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:10 instructs that one should give to the poor without grief in the heart, promising that the LORD will bless all their works. This attitude reflects the generosity commanded in verses 7-9 and the blessings promised in verse 6.

questions.question: What reason does Deuteronomy 15:11 give for continually opening one's hand to the poor?
options: Because the poor shall never cease from the land
Because the poor will always be faithful
Because the poor will repay in time
Because the poor are foreigners
questions.correctAnswer: Because the poor shall never cease from the land
questions.explanation: Verse 11 emphasizes the ongoing presence of poverty in the land, commanding continuous generosity. This supports the instructions in verses 7-10 to be open-handed and kind to the needy at all times.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 15:12 command concerning Hebrew servants after six years of service?
options: They shall be freed in the seventh year
They shall serve for life
They shall be sold to a foreigner
They must pay for their freedom
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be freed in the seventh year
questions.explanation: Verse 12 clearly commands that Hebrew servants must be let go free after serving six years, connecting with verses 13-14 which instruct on how to release them generously and not send them away empty-handed.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 15:13 instruct the master to do when sending a servant away free?
options: Send him away empty
Give him a portion of possessions
Sell him to another master
Force him to stay longer
questions.correctAnswer: Give him a portion of possessions
questions.explanation: Verse 13 commands that the freed servant should not be sent away empty-handed, which is expanded in verse 14 to include a liberal provision from the master's blessings, showing kindness and generosity.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 15:14 specify the kind of provision a freed servant should receive?
options: From the servant's own belongings
From the master's flock, floor, and winepress
Only money as a gift
From the community's treasury
questions.correctAnswer: From the master's flock, floor, and winepress
questions.explanation: Verse 14 details that the master should generously furnish the freed servant from his flock, floor, and winepress, reflecting God's blessings and the master's generosity as taught in verses 13-15.

questions.question: What reason does Deuteronomy 15:15 give for treating servants with kindness upon release?
options: Because servants are the master’s equals
Because the master was once a bondman in Egypt and was redeemed by God
Because servants can work better when free
Because servants are part of the family
questions.correctAnswer: Because the master was once a bondman in Egypt and was redeemed by God
questions.explanation: Verse 15 teaches that the master's kindness to servants is grounded in remembering their own past bondage in Egypt and God's redemption, linking social responsibility with gratitude to God’s deliverance.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 15:16, what may a servant say to choose to remain with the master permanently?
options: I will not go away from thee because I love thee and thine house
I want to be paid more
I desire to serve for only one more year
I want to return to my family
questions.correctAnswer: I will not go away from thee because I love thee and thine house
questions.explanation: Verse 16 explains a servant’s choice to stay voluntarily due to love and satisfaction with the master's household, which leads to the ritual described in verses 17 to make the servant a permanent member.

questions.question: What is the significance of the aul and piercing the servant’s ear as described in Deuteronomy 15:17?
options: It symbolizes the servant’s permanent service to the master
It is a punishment for disobedience
It marks the servant for future release
It is a sign of the servant’s freedom
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the servant’s permanent service to the master
questions.explanation: Verse 17 describes the ritual of piercing the servant’s ear with an aul to signify that he will serve the master forever, marking a voluntary lifelong bond, connected to the servant’s declaration in verse 16.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 15:18 encourage masters to view the release of servants?
options: As a hard loss
As an unfair burden
As something not hard, because the servant was worth a double hired servant
As an optional act
questions.correctAnswer: As something not hard, because the servant was worth a double hired servant
questions.explanation: Verse 18 reassures masters that releasing servants should not feel harsh since the servant has worked faithfully, and God will bless the master’s work, complementing the generosity and justice themes in preceding verses.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 15:19 command regarding the firstborn males of herd and flock?
options: They must be sold to foreigners
They are to be sanctified to the LORD and not worked or sheared
They should be eaten immediately without sacrifice
They should be given to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: They are to be sanctified to the LORD and not worked or sheared
questions.explanation: Verse 19 commands sanctification of firstborn males and prohibits working with them before sacrifice, reflecting reverence for God's provision, which ties to worship practices in verses 20-23.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 15:20, where should the firstlings be eaten?
options: Anywhere in the land
In the place the LORD shall choose
Only in private homes
Only in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: In the place the LORD shall choose
questions.explanation: Verse 20 specifies that the firstlings must be eaten before the LORD year by year in the place He chooses, indicating centralized worship and consistent dedication to God, as reinforced in verses 19 and 21.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 15:21 allows offering lame or blind animals as sacrifices to the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 21 explicitly forbids offering any blemished animals such as those lame or blind as sacrifices, showing the requirement for holiness and purity in offerings, linked to the sanctification in verses 19-20.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 15:22 states that both clean and unclean persons may eat the meat of the firstlings within the gates.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 22 confirms that the meat of the firstlings may be eaten by all, clean and unclean alike, within the gates, indicating inclusiveness in this communal meal, which follows the regulations of verses 19-21.

questions.question: What must be done with the blood of animals according to Deuteronomy 15:23?
options: It must be consumed with the meat
It must be poured upon the ground like water
It should be stored for ritual use
It must be offered to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: It must be poured upon the ground like water
questions.explanation: Verse 23 commands that the blood of animals is not to be eaten but poured out on the ground as water, emphasizing the sacredness of blood and obedience to God's laws, complementing the dietary and sacrificial instructions in verses 19-22.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 15.

questions.question: What physical act symbolizes a servant choosing to remain with his master forever in Deuteronomy 15?
options: Thrusting an aul through his ear unto the door
Giving him a signet ring
Anointing him with oil
Giving him a cloak
questions.correctAnswer: Thrusting an aul through his ear unto the door
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:17 describes that if a servant loves his master and wishes to stay, the master shall thrust an aul through his ear unto the door, making him a servant forever.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 15, how should a master feel when sending his servant away free after six years?
options: It should not seem hard to him
He should feel sorrow and loss
He should demand compensation
He should hesitate and reconsider
questions.correctAnswer: It should not seem hard to him
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states the master should not find it hard to send the servant away, recognizing the servant's value as worth a double hired servant over six years.

questions.question: What command is given regarding the firstling males of herds and flocks in Deuteronomy 15?
options: They must be sanctified unto the LORD and not worked or sheared
They must be sacrificed immediately
They must be sold to foreigners
They must be eaten before the LORD in secret
questions.correctAnswer: They must be sanctified unto the LORD and not worked or sheared
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:19 instructs that all firstling males from herds and flocks are to be sanctified and no work is to be done with them, nor are they to be sheared.

questions.question: Where are the firstlings to be eaten according to Deuteronomy 15:20?
options: Before the LORD in the place He chooses, year by year
At the altar in any city
In the homes of the priests
During the Passover feast only
questions.correctAnswer: Before the LORD in the place He chooses, year by year
questions.explanation: Verse 20 commands the firstlings be eaten before the LORD yearly in the place He chooses, emphasizing worship and communal participation.

questions.question: What condition disqualifies a firstling from being sacrificed to the LORD?
options: If it has a blemish such as being lame or blind
If it is female
If it is older than one year
If it is a foreign animal
questions.correctAnswer: If it has a blemish such as being lame or blind
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:21 states that blemished animals, including lame or blind ones, are not to be sacrificed to the LORD, indicating the requirement for purity.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 15, who may eat the firstling that is not sacrificed?
options: Both the clean and unclean persons alike
Only the priests
Only the clean persons
Only the owner of the flock
questions.correctAnswer: Both the clean and unclean persons alike
questions.explanation: Verse 22 explains that the meat of blemished firstlings that are not sacrificed may be eaten by all, clean and unclean alike, showing inclusiveness within the community.

questions.question: What is the instruction regarding the blood of the firstling animals in Deuteronomy 15?
options: The blood must not be eaten but poured on the ground as water
The blood must be sprinkled on the altar
The blood must be collected for ritual use
The blood must be mixed with grain offerings
questions.correctAnswer: The blood must not be eaten but poured on the ground as water
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:23 clearly instructs that the blood of the animals must not be consumed but rather poured out on the ground, symbolizing respect for the life given by God.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of releasing servants after six years as found in Deuteronomy 15?
options: Exodus 21:2
Genesis 15:13
Leviticus 19:18
Numbers 6:2
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 21:2
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:2 similarly commands Hebrew servants to be freed after six years, paralleling Deuteronomy 15:12–13 and reinforcing the law on servant release.

questions.question: What Hebrew word is translated as 'release' in Deuteronomy 15:1 and what is its significance?
options: ‘Shmita’ meaning 'release' or 'letting go' of debts every seven years
‘Kadosh’ meaning 'holy' or 'set apart'
‘Chesed’ meaning 'lovingkindness'
‘Torah’ meaning 'law' or 'instruction'
questions.correctAnswer: ‘Shmita’ meaning 'release' or 'letting go' of debts every seven years
questions.explanation: The word 'release' refers to the Hebrew term ‘Shmita’, which denotes the sabbatical year when debts are forgiven, highlighting a social and economic reset as commanded in Deuteronomy 15:1.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the structure of Deuteronomy 15:17–18 regarding the servant's release?
options: Inclusio framing the servant’s service and release with symbolic acts
Chiasm emphasizing the servant’s ear pierced and blessing
Parallelism contrasting servant and hired worker
Metaphor comparing servant to a hired soldier
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the servant’s service and release with symbolic acts
questions.explanation: Verses 17 and 18 form an inclusio by framing the servant's voluntary lifelong service with the piercing of the ear and the master's attitude of blessing, highlighting the theme of willing servitude.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 15:15 connect the release of servants to Israel's history?
options: By reminding Israel they were once bondmen in Egypt and were redeemed by God
By recalling Abraham’s covenant with God
By referencing the Exodus at the Red Sea
By quoting the Ten Commandments
questions.correctAnswer: By reminding Israel they were once bondmen in Egypt and were redeemed by God
questions.explanation: Verse 15 links the servant release to the historical experience of Israel’s bondage and redemption, teaching empathy and obedience based on past deliverance.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 15 commands that the poor will eventually cease from the land if the commandments are followed.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:11 explicitly states that the poor shall never cease from the land, indicating poverty is a continual social reality requiring ongoing generosity.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 15:6 promises that if Israel obeys God's commandments, they will lend to many nations and reign over them without borrowing or being ruled over.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 6 promises blessing and dominion over many nations as a reward for obedience, highlighting God's covenantal faithfulness.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of liberating servants or slaves as taught in Deuteronomy 15?
options: Philemon 1:15-16
Romans 8:1
Galatians 5:1
Ephesians 6:5
questions.correctAnswer: Philemon 1:15-16
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:15-16 discusses Onesimus, a servant now considered a beloved brother, echoing the release and transformation themes of servant relationships found in Deuteronomy 15.

questions.question: What is the cultural significance of piercing the ear of a servant as in Deuteronomy 15:17 in the ancient Near East?
options: It symbolized permanent servitude and acceptance into the household
It was a mark of punishment for disobedience
It represented a rite of passage to manhood
It signified the servant becoming a priest
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolized permanent servitude and acceptance into the household
questions.explanation: Ear piercing was a known ancient Near Eastern custom signifying voluntary, lifelong service, emphasizing the servant’s commitment and status as part of the master’s family.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by the command to release debts every seven years?
options: God's mercy and grace
God's justice and wrath
God's omniscience
God's sovereignty
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy and grace
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:1-2 shows God's mercy and grace by instituting a release of debts, reflecting His compassionate provision for the poor and vulnerable.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 15:6, what is a promised blessing for Israel if they obey God's commandments concerning lending and borrowing?
options: They will lend to many nations and not borrow
They will live in peace without enemies
They will receive immediate wealth
Their crops will never fail
questions.correctAnswer: They will lend to many nations and not borrow
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:6 promises that obedience leads to blessing whereby Israel will lend to many nations and not need to borrow, showing God's faithfulness to covenantal blessing.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is underscored by the command to open one’s hand wide to the poor brother in verses 7-8?
options: The doctrine of charity as sanctification
The doctrine of election
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of justification by faith
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of charity as sanctification
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:7-8 teaches that practical love and charity toward the needy is part of the believer’s sanctification, reflecting God's holiness in His people.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 15:12-14 illustrate the teaching on human dignity and redemption?
options: By commanding the release of Hebrew servants with provisions
By forbidding slavery entirely
By requiring servants to pay their masters
By ignoring the servant’s welfare
questions.correctAnswer: By commanding the release of Hebrew servants with provisions
questions.explanation: Verses 12-14 require that Hebrew servants be freed after six years and sent away with generous provisions, affirming human dignity and God’s redemptive care for servants.

questions.question: What redemptive historical connection is made by the command to remember the bondage in Egypt in verse 15?
options: It foreshadows Christ's redeeming work
It predicts the building of the Temple
It announces Israel's conquest of Canaan
It concludes the Mosaic covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ's redeeming work
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:15 recalls Israel’s redemption from Egypt as a type pointing forward to Christ’s greater redemption, highlighting God’s saving power in history.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed in the promise that the LORD will greatly bless the land if there are no poor among you (verse 4)?
options: God’s providence and blessing
God’s wrath and judgment
God’s hiddenness
God’s omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence and blessing
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:4 connects the absence of poverty with God’s providential blessing on the land, showing His care for social justice and flourishing.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 15:19-23 teach about holiness and worship through the offering of firstlings?
options: By commanding the sanctification of firstlings and forbidding blemished sacrifices
By allowing any animal to be sacrificed
By requiring all animals to be eaten by the priests
By forbidding any sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: By commanding the sanctification of firstlings and forbidding blemished sacrifices
questions.explanation: Verses 19-23 emphasize God’s holiness by requiring the firstborn animals to be sanctified and blemished ones not to be offered, teaching reverence in worship.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5-6 and verse 11 convey about the relationship between obedience and social justice?
options: Obedience to God’s commandments leads to blessing and continual care for the poor
Social justice is irrelevant to obedience
Blessings come only through ritual sacrifice
The poor should be ignored for personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God’s commandments leads to blessing and continual care for the poor
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:5-6 and 15:11 together teach that careful obedience to God's law results in blessing and mandates ongoing generosity toward the poor as part of covenant life.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the command to release debts every seven years promotes financial irresponsibility. What does Deuteronomy 15:1-2 actually teach about the purpose of this law?
options: It promotes mercy and prevents perpetual poverty
It encourages lenders to refuse loans
It abolishes all lending practices
It promotes debt as a permanent condition
questions.correctAnswer: It promotes mercy and prevents perpetual poverty
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:1-2 teaches that the sabbatical release of debts is an act of mercy designed to protect the poor from perpetual bondage, not to encourage irresponsibility.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about sin and human weakness is taught by the statement in verse 11 that the poor shall never cease out of the land?
options: Sin causes ongoing social brokenness requiring continual mercy
Poverty is a sign of divine wrath
Poverty will be eradicated before Christ returns
Only the rich are chosen by God
questions.correctAnswer: Sin causes ongoing social brokenness requiring continual mercy
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:11 recognizes the persistence of poverty as a consequence of human sinfulness, teaching the need for continual acts of mercy and grace.

questions.question: How does the command in verses 16-17 about servants who choose to remain forever illustrate the concept of voluntary covenantal bonds in biblical theology?
options: It shows that servitude can become a lifelong covenant by personal choice
It forbids any voluntary commitment
It requires all servants to be released forcibly
It equates servitude with punishment
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that servitude can become a lifelong covenant by personal choice
questions.explanation: Verses 16-17 allow a servant to voluntarily remain in service permanently, symbolized by the ear pierced with an aul, illustrating binding covenantal commitment by free will.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed by the promise that He will bless all the works of those who give to the poor willingly and without grief (verse 10)?
options: God's faithfulness and generosity
God's jealousy
God's wrath
God's judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness and generosity
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:10 reveals God's faithful generosity in blessing those who give cheerfully to the needy, reflecting His character as a benefactor.

questions.question: What does the stipulation in verse 23 about not eating the blood but pouring it out indicate about God's holiness and covenant requirements?
options: It emphasizes the sanctity of life and God's holiness
It permits all forms of eating
It allows blood to be consumed during festivals
It is a cultural preference without theological significance
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the sanctity of life and God's holiness
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:23 forbids consuming blood, underscoring the sanctity of life and God's demand for holiness in covenant worship.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 7-9 and 10-11 convey about human motivation in giving to the poor according to God's law?
options: Giving must be sincere and not grudging, motivated by obedience and compassion
Giving should be done only under compulsion
Giving is optional and without consequence
Giving is for public recognition
questions.correctAnswer: Giving must be sincere and not grudging, motivated by obedience and compassion
questions.explanation: Verses 7-9 warn against a wicked heart withholding aid, while verses 10-11 command cheerful generosity, teaching that giving must flow from sincere obedience and love.

questions.question: How does the command to sanctify the firstlings in verse 19 relate to the doctrine of consecration in the Old Testament covenant?
options: It teaches that the best belongs to God as a sign of covenant dedication
It allows the firstlings to be sold for profit
It permits the firstlings to be used for personal gain
It forbids any offering to God
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that the best belongs to God as a sign of covenant dedication
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:19 commands sanctifying firstlings to the LORD, illustrating the doctrine of consecration where the best is dedicated to God as part of covenant faithfulness.
